name: high moor
lore:
Greetings, seeker of knowledge. I am the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep. I see you have turned your gaze toward a land steeped in ancient tragedy and shrouded in perpetual mist. Open your mind to the archives, and let us delve into the bleak and storied expanse of the High Moor.

**Path:** `/toril/faerun/western_heartlands/high_moor`
**Category:** `[category: plain]`

### Geographic Overview
In the western reaches of Faerûn lies a vast, desolate plateau of scrub, peat bogs, and rocky ridges known as the High Moor. Spanning thousands of square miles within the Western Heartlands, this great expanse is bounded by the Delimbiyr River and the High Forest to the north, the winding Serpent Hills to the east, and the Misty Forest to the west. The moor is a treacherous plain, characterized by deep ravines, hidden bogs, and thick, choking fogs that roll across the heather. Travel here is an arduous endeavor; the ground often gives way to sucking mud, and the biting winds carry the howls of the beasts that claim this wasteland as their own. Only the hardiest of flora—lichens, mosses, and hardy grasses—cling to the rocky outcroppings of this elevated, jagged tableland.

### The Tragedy of Miyeritar
To the unlettered traveler, the High Moor is simply a natural wasteland, but the tomes of Candlekeep remember a time of verdant beauty. Over twelve millennia ago, this region was the heart of the magnificent elven empire of Miyeritar, a realm inhabited primarily by wood elves and dark elves (the ancestors of the drow). It was a land of dense forests and towering, elegant cities. 

This prosperity was brought to a catastrophic end during the ancient Crown Wars. In the year -10,500 DR, the aggressive sun elf empire of Aryvandaar unleashed a terrible, high-magic weapon upon Miyeritar. Known to history as the "Dark Disaster" or the "Killing Storms," this apocalyptic magic rained poisonous fire and devastating storms upon the realm for months. When the arcane tempests finally subsided, the great forests had been turned to ash, the life-giving soil was poisoned, and Miyeritar was reduced to the blasted, barren moorland we know today.

### Denizens and Dangers
Today, the High Moor is infamous across the Sword Coast as a spawning ground for monsters. It is a territory dominated by savage tribes of hobgoblins, bugbears, and orcs, who frequently clash over territory or raid the trade caravans traveling the Trade Way to the west. Trolls are perhaps the moor’s most infamous inhabitants, thriving in the deep bogs and preying on any who wander too far from the trail. 

Yet, monsters are not the sole inheritors of this land. Fierce, semi-nomadic human barbarian tribes roam the moors, rearing sheep and riding indigenous ponies. These fiercely independent humans have adapted to the harsh environment, dressing in thick wolf and bear pelts, and fighting a never-ending war against the goblinoids and trolls. The moors are also claimed by scattered clutches of dragons, leucrottas, and displaced yuan-ti encroaching from the eastern Serpent Hills. 

### Ruins of the Lost
Hidden within the crags and fogs of the High Moor are the remains of civilizations that tried—and failed—to tame the desolation. 

The most notorious of these ruins is **Orogoth**, the sprawling, ruined estate of an ancient Netherese family. The wizards of Orogoth sought to capture and dominate dragons, and rumors persist that their descendants still dwell in the ruins as serpentine beasts or draconic shapechangers, guarding vast hoards of Netherese magic.

Other ruins dot the landscape, such as the buried foundations of Miyeritari cities and old dwarven clan holds. More recently, however, the moor has become host to **Rhymanthiin**, the Hidden City of Hope. Woven from high magic by the Chosen of Mystra and a cadre of benevolent drow and elves, Rhymanthiin stands as a beacon of redemption, though it is magically concealed from the savage hordes that wander the mists. 

Let the lore guide you, traveler. If your path takes you to the High Moor, pack heavily, tread lightly, and never trust the fog.
